51576435.protein: Nuclear receptor subfamily 4 group A member 2
51576435.DESCRIPTION: Binding affinity to recombinant N-terminal 6His-tagged Nurr1 LBD (362 to 598 residues) (unknown origin) expressed in Escherichia coli BL21(DE3)-R3-pRARE2 cells assessed as dissociation constant at 100 uM by ITC analysis

original_paragraph.Materials and Methods - Isothermal Titra: Isothermal Titration Calorimetry. ITC experiments for ligand binding to Nurr1 were conducted on an Affinity ITC instrument (TA Instruments, New Castle, DE) at 25 °C with a stirring rate of 75 rpm. Nurr1 LBD protein (10–20 μM) in buffer (20 mM Tris pH 7.5, 100 mM NaCl, 5% glycerol) containing 3% or 4% DMSO was titrated with the test compounds (100 μM in the same buffer containing 3% or 4% DMSO) in 21–26 injections (1 × 1 μL and 20 × 4 to 25 × 4 μL) with an injection interval of 150–180 s. As control experiments, the test compounds were titrated to the buffer, and the buffer was titrated to the Nurr1 LBD protein under otherwise identical conditions. The heat rates of the compound-Nurr1 LBD titrations were analyzed using NanoAnalyze software (TA Instruments, New Castle, DE) with an independent binding model.
original_paragraph.Figure 5 caption: Figure 5. In vitro profiling of NR4A modulators 108, 110, and 111. (a) Isothermal titration calorimetry demonstrated high-affinity binding of 108, 110, and 111 to the Nurr1 LBD. The fittings of the heat of binding are shown, and the isotherms at 25 °C are shown as insets. (b) Selectivity profiling of 108, 110, and 111 on FAM-binding nuclear receptors. Data are the mean ± SEM fold activation of the respective nuclear receptors in Gal4-hybrid reporter gene assays; n = 3. Reference ligands are described in the experimental section. (c) Activity of 108, 110, and 111 on NR4A receptors. Data are the mean ± SEM, n ≥ 3. (d) Effects of 110 and 111 on full-length human Nurr1 on the human response elements NBRE (monomer), NurRE (homodimer), and DR5 (heterodimer). Data are the mean ± SEM, n ≥ 3.
